purpose: Structure the autonomous run as a portfolio of PRODUCT workstreams rather than a stream of small tweaks. Every experiment declares a workstream, expected information value, scope, and the mechanism it tests. Reviewed globally every 60-90 minutes. Product north star: docs/PRODUCT_NORTH_STAR.md. What is measurable and by what command: docs/METRIC_COVERAGE_MATRIX.md.

antiRepetitionRule.justificationMustArgue: why a third experiment on substantially the same mechanism has greater information value than switching workstreams

workstreams.name: measurement / evaluation validity
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Whether the repaired synthetic construct measures anything that transfers to real people. The generator now produces semantically coherent language and the availability denominator is stance-aware and extractor-independent, but the whole target is still synthetic: no human-labelled preference truth exists.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: With backwards polarity, positional bias, late-sentence loss, and duplicate evidence paths removed, DEVELOPMENT metrics are now valid RELATIVE measures for comparing decoders, and remain invalid as absolute claims about human preference recovery.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: AVAILABLE_EVIDENCE_PREFERENCE_MACRO_MAE_V1 as primary, always published with RECOGNIZED_* macro/micro, AVAILABLE_TO_RECOGNIZED_RECALL, ZERO_AVAILABLE_EVIDENCE_MAE, LEGACY_ALL_DIMENSION_MAE, constant-5, development prior, and the shrinkage curve.
workstreams.strongestFailedAlternative: AUTONOMOUS_OBSERVED_PREFERENCE_MACRO_MAE_V1, whose inclusion set was gated on extractor recognition. It let the algorithm shrink its own denominator by missing evidence. Superseded, still reported for comparison.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Preregistered metric-contract review of integration_preference. Its exclusion from AUTONOMOUS_PREFERENCE_DIMENSIONS_V1 was justified solely by ~4% generator coverage, but that 4% was an artifact of the positional sampling bias fixed in the preflight: at position 12 in DIMENSION_IDS it was almost never reached by filter-then-slice. Measured coverage under unbiased sampling is 0.2933, well above the 0.10 floor, and it passes every non-coverage monotonicity criterion. Promoting it would take the eligible set from 2 dimensions to 3, materially widening the only construct-valid measurement surface the project has. Deliberately NOT applied in the preflight because changing the eligible set is a metric-contract change, not a decoder experiment.
workstreams.secondNextExperiment: Establish whether directional accuracy among LEANING predictions (now reported separately from raw directionalAccuracy) is a better primary construct than continuous MAE, given that MAE is dominated by how often the decoder sits on the neutral prior.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: None yet: this workstream was just substantially repaired. Re-assess after the first two experiments.
openBlockers: No independent human preference truth. Absolute validity claims are out of scope for autonomous work.

workstreams.name: preference representation + extraction
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Whether a 17-dimension bipolar vector is the right representation at all. Eight of the seventeen dimensions are classified as construct-invalid or overlapping in src/lab/preferenceTarget.ts, and only two are MAE-eligible.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: Extraction recall, not scoring arithmetic, is the binding constraint. AVAILABLE_TO_RECOGNIZED_RECALL is about 0.31: the regex/lexicon extractor misses roughly two thirds of the preference language the generator exposes, so predictions stay pinned near the neutral prior and prediction variance is under 10% of truth variance.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Regex evidence classes (src/domain/evidence.ts) over a work-structure lexicon (src/domain/workStructure.ts), with explicit-list stance forcing.
workstreams.strongestFailedAlternative: Not yet attempted at a family level. The lexicon has only been extended, never replaced.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Replace lexical phrase matching with embedding retrieval at the preference_evidence_extraction boundary and measure AVAILABLE_TO_RECOGNIZED_RECALL. This is an ARCHITECTURAL-scope test of a different family, not a lexicon extension.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: Adding lexicon entries has repeatedly moved recall a few points without changing the variance-collapse picture. Further additive lexicon work is explicitly deprioritized.

workstreams.name: experience representation / extraction
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Whether performed work can be recovered from compressed first-person resume language at all. Person-side Task mapping is 0.194 exact Top-1 at the hard tier against 0.870 on the job side.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: The asymmetry is caused by surface form, not by the canonical model: resume bullets compress and reframe, job postings do not. Short text (<=12 words) drops to 0.322 Top-1 with 31% abstention while long text reaches 0.920.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Evidence-class regexes plus the shared lexical mapper (src/domain/evidence.ts, src/v3/mapper.ts).
workstreams.strongestFailedAlternative: None at a family level. The extractor lexicon has only been extended, never replaced.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Close the person/job mapping asymmetry. Test whether a query-expansion or embedding step on the PERSON side alone raises person_experience exactTop1Accuracy without touching the job side. This is the single largest measured gap in the pipeline.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: Extraction macro F1 falls from 0.831 on DEVELOPMENT paraphrase families to 0.611 on withheld VALIDATION families: additive regex work is already overfitting to phrasing.

workstreams.name: Task/DWA mapping
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Whether token-overlap retrieval over 12,579 O*NET task statements can distinguish genuinely different work, or whether it mostly matches shared generic vocabulary.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: Lexical retrieval gives adequate recall for candidate generation but poor precision on broad DWAs; a reranking stage is where precision must come from.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Deterministic lexical retrieval (topK=5) with a task/DWA/abstain threshold policy. Now 55x faster after hoisting corpus tokenization, and memoized by cacheKey.
workstreams.strongestFailedAlternative: None recorded. The CandidateReranker seam exists but no reranker has been wired.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Wire a cross-encoder or selective LLM reranker at the contextual_reranking boundary and measure precision on the ambiguity/broad-collision fixtures, with abstention rate as a guardrail.
openBlockers: No human-labelled mapping truth. Mapping ACCURACY cannot be established autonomously; only relative behaviour on known-answer fixtures.

workstreams.name: job responsibility extraction and mapping
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Job-side Task mapping is strong (0.870 Top-1) but never abstains, and when it falls back to DWA it picks the right DWA only 12% of the time. And free-text responsibility segmentation does not exist at all.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: The DWA fallback is close to worthless as implemented: it takes the top candidate's FIRST DWA rather than selecting among DWAs. Fixing selection may be worth more than improving Task-level retrieval.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Structured responsibility list plus the shared lexical mapper.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Test whether DWA fallback should SELECT among the candidate's DWAs rather than taking the first, measured by dwaHierarchicalAccuracy on job_responsibility. Cheap, mechanism-level, and currently at 0.120.
openBlockers: Free-text JD segmentation is not implemented and is excluded from the loop (contract row 8).

workstreams.name: Experience Fit and transferable-job discovery
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Whether the canonical Task/DWA path can beat a naive bag-of-words resume-to-JD baseline on experience ranking at all. At the hard tier TaskDNA scores 0.937 experience NDCG@5 against resume-lexical's 0.963: a lift of -0.026. TaskDNA's measurable advantage is confined to cross-title (+0.042), cross-industry (+0.083) and surprising-transfer (+0.042) recall.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: Upstream mapping is the constraint, not the ranking arithmetic. Person mapping recovers only 0.194 of planted Tasks, so ranking works with a fraction of the available signal while the lexical baseline uses the whole text. If mapping recall rises, the canonical path should overtake the baseline; if it does not, the canonical representation is the wrong bottleneck to be optimizing.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Exact-Task and DWA identity matching with strength and ownership weights (src/v3/fit.ts experienceFit).
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Establish whether the negative lift is caused by mapping recall or by information loss in canonicalization. Hold ranking fixed and feed the scorer PERFECT mappings (planted atoms directly) to get the ceiling; compare against the current 0.937. If the perfect-mapping ceiling exceeds resume-lexical, mapping recall is the target (workstream 3/12). If it does not, canonicalization itself is discarding information the baseline keeps, which is an ARCHITECTURAL finding.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: None yet on this evaluator, but the negative lift is itself evidence that further ranking-arithmetic work is not the priority.
openBlockers: Human relevance judgement of person-job pairs is required for a product claim.

workstreams.name: Preference Fit and joint Experience/Preference discovery
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Preference is the weakest ranking channel at 0.618 hard-tier NDCG, and a job with equal liked and disliked work scores exactly the neutral 0.5 -- indistinguishable from a job with no preference evidence. Mode B's Pareto plus maximin ordering also drops preference NDCG to 0.349 from the 0.618 the single-channel ranking achieves, so the joint policy is currently paying for experience with preference.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: The mean-based aggregation in preferenceFit is the problem: it lets liked and disliked work cancel. A separate liked-coverage and disliked-intrusion pair may carry more product meaning than one signed mean.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Signed mean of stance contributions centred at 0.5 (src/v3/fit.ts preferenceFit).
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Test whether reporting liked coverage and disliked intrusion as two numbers, instead of one cancelling mean, raises preference NDCG and removes the MIXED_PREFERENCE ambiguity. This is a REPRESENTATION change, not a coefficient change.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: None yet: this evaluator is new.
openBlockers: Whether a preference score predicts real satisfaction needs longitudinal human outcomes.

workstreams.name: Direction Fit and career transitions
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Direction is the least-evidenced channel: 0.769 hard-tier NDCG with 3 of 12 people below the catastrophe threshold, driven by 0.542 mapping abstention on aspiration language.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: Aspiration framings put the most surface distance between the statement and the canonical task, so the mapper abstains. Direction quality is currently a mapping problem, not a scoring problem.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Aspiration mapping plus mapped-alignment scoring (src/v3/fit.ts directionFit).
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Measure whether stripping the aspirational frame before mapping (mapping the work phrase rather than the whole sentence) raises person_direction exactTop1Accuracy. Mechanism: frame removal, not threshold tuning.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: None yet: this evaluator is new.
openBlockers: Stated direction may differ from revealed direction.

workstreams.name: Qualification Fit
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Ambiguous education and credential equivalence cannot be solved by a fixed alias table. Hard-gap precision and recall are currently 1.0 only because requirements are structured and exact.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: The measured 1.0 is plumbing correctness, not equivalence capability. Any realistic requirement set would break it immediately.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Exact-plus-alias matching with a preferred-requirement weight (src/v3/fit.ts qualificationFit).
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Introduce paraphrased and abbreviated requirement values into the planted corpus (BSc vs bachelor degree, JS vs JavaScript) and measure how far hard-gap precision falls. That establishes the real baseline before any equivalence component is built.
openBlockers: Regulated credential equivalence has a legal answer no model should invent.
Free-text qualification extraction is excluded from the loop (contract row 4).

workstreams.name: candidate retrieval
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Canonical-work retrieval recall COLLAPSES to 0.540 at the hard tier while plain lexical overlap holds 0.868. The canonical path is less robust to compressed language than the naive one it was meant to beat.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: Retrieval recall is an upper bound on every downstream ranking metric, so this is currently the most damaging single number in the pipeline. A hybrid (lexical union canonical) should dominate either alone.
workstreams.strongestFailedAlternative: Title-only retrieval, decisively: 0.444 recall and 0.0 cross-title recall.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Test a hybrid retriever that unions lexical and canonical candidates, measured by candidateRecallAtK at the hard tier with title/stratum/industry concentration as guardrails. Highest information value in the whole portfolio right now.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: None yet, but canonical retrieval being 0.33 recall BELOW the naive lexical retriever it was meant to beat is the strongest single signal in the portfolio.
openBlockers: Live posting ingestion, freshness and closed-job detection are out of scope for this loop.

workstreams.name: robustness / leakage / generalization
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Extraction macro F1 drops 0.831 -> 0.611 between DEVELOPMENT and withheld VALIDATION paraphrase families. Gains may be phrasing-specific.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: The regex evidence lexicon is tuned to the framings DEVELOPMENT contains. Ranking is less affected because it leans on job-side mapping, which is robust.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Withheld paraphrase families per split, the verbatim/standard/hard difficulty ladder, and explicit leakage tests.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Withhold whole OCCUPATIONS and occupation FAMILIES from DEVELOPMENT, not just paraphrase families, and re-measure the gap. Paraphrase-family withholding is a coarse generalization test.

workstreams.name: architecture / model capacity / contextual reasoning
workstreams.largestUncertainty: Whether the person-side mapping ceiling is a lexical-representation limit rather than a tuning limit.
workstreams.currentHypothesis: It is a representation limit. Lexical overlap cannot bridge a 0.19 token-overlap paraphrase, and the person/job asymmetry (0.194 vs 0.870) tracks surface distance almost exactly. This is the strongest available evidence for trying a different family.
workstreams.currentBestStrategy: Token-overlap lexical retrieval with no reranker wired.
workstreams.strongestFailedAlternative: None: no alternative family has been implemented yet.
workstreams.highestValueNextExperiment: Implement ONE alternative at the contextual_reranking boundary (cross-encoder or selective LLM) and measure RERANK_TOP1_DELTA_OVER_DETERMINISTIC on person_experience, under the declared invocation-rate and cost caps. Contract row 27 permits building then measuring; it forbids claiming a result before implementing one.
workstreams.diminishingReturnsEvidence: Additive lexicon and regex work has produced a measurable generalization gap without closing the person/job asymmetry: that is the diminishing-returns signal for the current family.
openBlockers: Any learned component must expose the full LearnedComponent contract including a deterministic fallback.

optimizationTarget.rationale: The standard difficulty tier saturates experience and direction NDCG at 1.000. Only the hard tier has headroom.

excludedFromLoop.reason: no JD segmenter exists; largest job-side coverage gap
no constraint fields exist in the data model; vacuous rather than passing
permanently excluded; no human annotation exists

headlineFinding.statement: At the declared optimization target (hard tier, 12 people, K=5), TaskDNA does NOT yet beat a naive bag-of-words resume-to-job-description baseline on its central claim. Experience NDCG@5 is 0.937 for TaskDNA against 0.963 for resume-lexical: a lift of -0.026. Canonical-work candidate retrieval recall is 0.540 against 0.868 for plain lexical overlap.
headlineFinding.whatTaskDNADoesWin: Cross-title transfer recall 0.958 vs 0.917 (+0.042), cross-industry transfer recall 0.917 vs 0.833 (+0.083), surprising-transfer recall 0.958 vs 0.917 (+0.042). It beats title-only (0.459 experience NDCG) and occupation-stratum (0.655) decisively, and it has a far lower same-title/different-work false-positive rate (0.017 vs 0.200 for occupation-stratum).
headlineFinding.interpretation: The canonical Task/DWA machinery is not yet earning its keep against a bag-of-words baseline on ranking, and is actively WORSE on retrieval. Its measurable advantage today is specifically cross-boundary discovery, which is the product thesis but a narrow slice of it. This is the single most important thing for the loop to work on and it is why workstreams 10 and 12 carry the highest information value.
